If you're considering launching a product on Product Hunt, keep watching. I joined Product Hunt in 2015. I've done two product launches in 2020 and 2024. The first time around, we didn't really know much. We launched it and it didn't go anywhere. The second time around, we Learned a good bit about how Product Hunt works, put in a lot of work and we got to number two product of the day and No. 5 product of the week. In fact, the same day we launched, Google launched Gemini on Product Hunt. And we finished ahead of Gemini. Just felt like a brag point worth sharing. But that experience also taught us that the game is rigged, and if you can rig the game in your favour, things will work out. So when Product Hunt first launched, it quickly became super popular in Silicon Valley and it was the norm to go launch your product on Product Hunt. And if you got one of these awards, it was a real brag worthy moment. And you also got a lot of R 0 I. A lot of people found your product, came and used it. You suddenly had a traffic surge. All good things happened over the years, especially as Silicon Valley went through its lull phase in technology, Product Hunt became a little bit of a ghost town. People only went there if they were launching their products, which means that no one's really incentivised to browsing and checking Out your product. They're all there to just support their mission. Which meant it really became a game of who could get more people to upload their product. The day we launched, there was one other company that was equally prepared, or maybe slightly better prepared than we were. Which means we got into a boarding war with them. And we basically kept toggling in number one, number two position all the way to the end of the night, when we finished second. In other words, it really helps if you can have an army ready to go and upload when you're launching. Now, there's nothing structurally wrong with this, because if you have a product, and if you have built a community around the product, and if you have early users, those are the people that should technically be uploading your product and supporting your launch. But at the end of the day, because of dwindling traffic, the real ROI was just a backlink. That really bumped up your SEO a little bit. And the brag worthy award badges that you can put on your website. But fast forward to today, there appears to be something changing in Product Hunt Energy, and it may have something to do with Silicon Valley buzzing again. But basically, I see a I.
